\begin{quote}
\textbf{Investment in the Future:} Consider two firms that play a Cournot competition game with demand \(p = 100 - q\) and costs for each firm given by \(c_i(q_i) = 10q_i\). Imagine that before the two firms play the Cournot game firm 1 can invest in cost reduction. If it invests the costs of firm 1 will drop to \(c_1(q_1) = 5q_1\). The cost of investment is \(F > 0\). Firm 2 does not have this investment opportunity.

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\alph{enumi}.}
\item
  Find the value \(F^*\) for which the unique subgame-perfect equilibrium involves firm 1 investing.
\item
  Assume that \(F > F^*\). Find a Nash equilibrium of the game that is not subgame perfect.
\end{enumerate}
\end{quote}
